tutorial: No tutorial: the eight BIM tools of the hub that bimcam-bim-model.json left in notCovered (bim_reference, bim_library, bim_image_plane, bim_reextrude, bim_remove_shape, bim_glue, bim_rewire, bim_nest). The house shell is the Arch tutorial's outer walls with one window, as bimcam-bim-model.json starts; each tool then gets the small thing it needs, set beside the house.

conventions.run: Agent Link for FreeCAD's batch, in order; { $from, $at } takes a value from an earlier call's answer (2 → 6, 8 → 9, 11 → 12 and 13). A runner that cuts the list into parts must keep each pair in one part or write the answer to a file (chain.py: an answer is not kept between parts).
conventions.sessionFolder: bim_library's folder and the three refusal paths are written as ~/AgentLink/…: the window link's session folder is ~/AgentLink (agentlink/gui_link.py). No answer gives a folder alone, and { $at } cannot cut a file name off a path, so the folder cannot be a reference. If the session's folder is another one, call 8 is refused 'No objects library here' (or finds nothing): put that folder in calls 8 to 10.
conventions.units: mm in; the gap tools answer volume in mm³ and box in mm (bim_wall and bim_structure answer volume_m3).
conventions.leftBehind: In the session's folder: bim-rest-lib/shelf-block.FCStd, bim-rest-plan.png, bim-rest-nest.png. Two unsaved documents stay open (BimRest, and shelf-block saved).

Run 5 answered failed ("FreeCAD's nester stopped"): with [0, 90] together FreeCAD's nester gives up on the whole run when one rotation leaves a piece room only where it would touch another. Since hubfix4 the tool then tries each rotation alone: the answer carries rotationsUsed ([0] or [90]) and rotationsNote beside rotations [0, 90], and the rest as above. notCovered: code_* (code_answer, code_check, code_facts, code_fem, code_missing, code_packet, code_packs, code_project, code_span): the private Home add-on's tools; its repository is not checked out where this model was written, so no call of them is here.

bim_reference { part } (one named part of the file) and an .ifc or .dxf file: the part's name is the object's internal name inside the other file ('Box' for the shelf block by FreeCAD's naming, not checked live); one live call bim_reference { path, part: "Box" } would say.
bim_library with the parts_library add-on itself (no folder given): it is not known to be installed on the Mac; with it, bim_library { search: "bolt" } alone answers found from its roots.
bim_reextrude on a panel (Thickness) or a structure, with delete: false, and from a face with a curved edge (wire false: the face itself becomes the base).
bim_remove_shape on a wall (a line and a new wall replace it) and on a shape that is not a box (left as it was, coloured red in the window by FreeCAD).
bim_rewire with an arc (a plain Part wire is made, not a Draft wire) and bim_nest with more pieces than fit one sheet (sheets over 1, with the note).
Which face of the wall Face6 is: not needed for the answer (see call 16), and shape_query { body: "Stub wall", kind: "face", normal: [0, 0, 1] } says if wanted.
